# Independent audit of the five-interval barrier and birth escape

PASS after reading `candidate dcd790485c83acdc` in full. I independently regenerated the complete rational cap-knot tables and derived both the fixed-support cone obstruction and the support-augmentation cap certificate.

## 1. Baseline and the full neighborhood

The baseline widths are (13,11,9,7,5), with mass45. Direct clamping at all listed knots gives minimum33/2 and complementary maximum57/2 at both source bases1,2. The source1 minimum is attained on the whole slope plateau [7/4,9/2]; its reverse has the corresponding negative plateau. The source2 minimum is the negative far plateau and its reverse is the positive far plateau. Pure base caps have a strict gap. The other source maxima are bounded by13/2,17/2,5/2, so the two displayed bases are the only deepest ones.

Under small changes of all interval endpoints, the old plateau statuses persist. On source1's plateau the derivative in base tilt is zero because the proper block is0,1,2, and its value at the adjusted mark y1=(c0+c1+c2)/3 is exactly (w0+w1+w2)/2. At source2 the outward saturated plateau has value w2/2+w3+w4 at its own interval center. The complete knot ordering and all noncritical gaps persist, so these are genuine all-normal lower certificates, not just four convenient cap upper bounds.

The four fixed-normal cap groups still cover every candidate plane: the left group's two margins sum to a negative multiple of z-1, and the right group's sum to a positive multiple of z-2. There is no integer between1 and2. Therefore the exact global depth in the whole neighborhood is max(q1,q2), including all candidate marks and every active-source switch.

The explicit endpoint neighborhood of radius1/100 is safe. The crude knot-mass error bound of .55 remains below the noncritical gap11/6 even if the comparison value M-q is allowed to shift by .15 rather than only the .05 possible for q alone. This is a wording clarification of the quoted error estimate, not a restriction of the neighborhood.

## 2. The fixed-support minimum and equality case

Concavity of the widths gives M<=5w2. Hence

    3 max(q1,q2)>=2q1+q2=M+w2/2>=11M/10.

Equality forces q1=q2 and equality in the concave-sequence midpoint inequalities. This makes all widths affine in their base index. The source tie then forces their ratio to be exactly13:11:9:7:5. The convex lower roof and concave upper roof have equal second differences when their width difference is affine; those second differences must both vanish. Thus centers are affine as well.

This proves the strict normalized local minimum modulo shear, translation, and positive continuous scaling. The resulting obstruction is stronger than a bad endpoint-rate choice. For additional verification, write a normalized concave width perturbation as

    delta w_i=alpha+b i-sum_(k=1)^3 c_k(i-k)_+,
    c_k>=0, sum_i delta w_i=0.

The two source variations are

    delta q1=-3b/2+13c1/10+9c2/10+3c3/10,
    delta q2=3b-5c1/2-3c2/2-c3/2.

Both can be nonpositive only if

    b >=(13c1+9c2+3c3)/15,
    b <=(5c1+3c2+c3)/6.

The lower bound exceeds the upper by (c1+3c2+c3)/30 unless all curvature parameters vanish. Then b=alpha=0. This independently confirms the equality rigidity used in the path argument.

The stated open-and-closed argument is valid after continuous normalization of total mass and removal of the affine center graph, as long as the five sampled fibers remain positive and their endpoints vary continuously. It does not prohibit paths which first change the complete sampled support; the note explicitly makes this distinction.

## 3. Point birth and exact descent

The preliminary path adjoins (-t,13/2+t) and (4+t,0). Both points lie in the wedge between the affine extensions of the original endpoint roofs. Thus every original integer fiber is squeezed between the same old interval and the same wedge section and is unchanged. Until t=1 there is no additional integer base; at t=1 the new fibers at -1 and5 are points of zero one-dimensional mass and zero depth. Mixed measure and maximum depth remain constant on the entire preliminary path.

Growing the new intervals as [15/2-u,15/2] and [-u/4,u/4], with0<=u<3, preserves the exact old fibers and complete support {-1,...,5}. The displayed roof slope inequalities are correct. Total mass is45+3u/2.

The left cap pair through (1,u/6) has old proper-block masses33/2-u/2 and33/2+u/2. The first captures the entire new left interval; the second misses it precisely under the sufficient condition u<3. Both miss the new right interval. Thus both total masses are33/2+u/2. The right pair through (2,0) misses the left new interval and captures the right one in both orientations, giving the same mass. Their two whole-plane coverage properties include EVERY new candidate, so no residual-depth or compactness argument is needed for the new bases.

Consequently

    beta_actual(u)<=(33/2+u/2)/(45+3u/2)<11/30

for every0<u<3. The derivative of this upper certificate is -9/[4(45+3u/2)^2]. At u=1 the upper bound is34/93, with exact improvement1/930. The source correctly refrains from claiming that the actual optimized depth is monotone between every pair of positive parameters merely because its upper certificate decreases.

This establishes the claimed exact obstruction and escape. It is not a general fiber-birth theorem and does not make the baseline body an OC counterexample: its initial depth11/30 is above1/4.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
